req_desc: The app presents the studio's published projects to a visitor who has not signed in ...
The app offers no customer account, no cart, no payment, no comments, no search.
An anonymous visitor reads every published route without signing in ...
A `reader` downloads the press kit of any published project ...
An `author` creates a project through the studio console.
Registration at `/signup` produces a `reader` account only.
The server refuses a mutating request made with a `reader` token against an author-only endpoint.
The app seeds the account `author@example.com` ...
A sign-in with a seeded email plus the correct password returns a bearer token ...
A request to an author-only endpoint carrying no token leaves the targeted state unchanged.
The header survives a route change ...
A route change updates the address bar to the destination path ...
A cold load of `/work` renders the work route directly.
The header carries the primary trio `Home`, `Work`, `Services` ...
Each of the three world clocks shows the current wall time in the named city ...
Every internal link on every public route resolves.
The footer carries the call to action `WE WOULD LOVE TO HEAR FROM YOU.` ...
The hero renders a drifting colour field behind the headline ...
The hero headline is selectable text rather than painted pixels ...
The hero words are readable before the animated field starts ...
The reel carries the eyebrow `RECENT WORK` ...
The reel holds the four seeded projects flagged `featured_home` ...
The reel closes on a pill reading `Discover all projects`.
The work filter bar carries the eight controls beginning `All`, `SPATIAL`, `Campaign`.
Choosing a work filter narrows the grid without a page reload ...
A work filter matching no published project shows the index empty state.
A project cover plays only when pointed at, pausing otherwise.
The press filter set carries a derived count beside each of `News`, `Events`, `Features`, `Articles` ...
The press feed lists items newest first ...
The series block carries the tag `Designing for the future` ...
The press route repeats the contact invitation as three pill links.
The team route opens on a three-line heading revealed line by line ...
The team banner draws in against the scroll rather than on entry.
The member grid closes on the derived count `11 members`.
The team route closes on the two dated chapters `2011`, `2019`.
An unknown address renders the heading `Page not found` ...
A valid enquiry submission stores the enquiry ...
An enquiry with an empty name writes no row ...
An enquiry carrying anything in the hidden field `company_website` is refused ...
The enquiry list at `/studio/enquiries` is served to an `author` alone.
The cookie rail states that the website uses cookies ...
No analytics tag loads before the cookie choice is accepted.
The app records each page view with the route plus the moment.
An anonymous request for a console path is sent to `/login` ...
Project creation runs as three steps, each at a separate address ...
Finishing the wizard lands on a full-page confirmation naming the new project ...
An uploaded cover lands in the bucket at `projects/{project_id}/{sha256_of_bytes}.{ext}` ...
Publishing a project makes the project visible on the public index ...
A draft project is absent from the work index ...
A draft project's cover object is served to an `author` alone ...
A press-kit object is served to a signed-in account alone ...
The app never makes a bucket publicly readable ...
The route `/sitemap.xml` lists every public route ...
The route `/robots.txt` names the sitemap address.
The app serves the route `/` as the hero plus reel ...
A successful sign-in lands on the path originally requested ...
The work grid under a filter matching nothing shows an empty state ...
The work route ground is a near-white neutral ...
A failure state wears a colour that appears nowhere else.
Meaning is never carried by colour alone ...
The site commits to one designed scheme with no second theme.
Display, body plus interface type is set in `Inter` ...
A swash letter is an inline element around one glyph rather than a change of family ...
Motion character across the whole site is eased ...
A reduced-motion request holds the hero on a still frame ...
The work grid runs two columns at desktop width ...
The studio console reads as a plain working surface rather than the public display register ...
The app reads the datastore address from `DATABASE_URL` ...
The app introduces no second datastore beyond PostgreSQL.
No credential appears in anything the browser downloads.
Every public route carries a title distinct from every other public route.
The build ships no image file ...
The hero pauses the hero loop when the tab is hidden ...
The schema holds a `projects` table carrying a `status` field ...
The schema holds a `press_items` table carrying a `category` field ...
The schema holds an `enquiries` table carrying a `source` field.
The member count is computed on read rather than stored.
Every seeded account uses the password `deku-demo-pw-2026` ...
The seed carries eight published projects plus one draft ...
Restarting the app duplicates no seeded row.
The palette is exposed as custom properties named on the document root ...
Body type resolves to `16px` over `18.4px` ...
The wordmark is drawn by the app rather than loaded ...
The marker between a client plus a piece stays the typed character `‣`.
The not-found route carries no reveal, no parallax.
The app serves a single studio with no second tenant ...
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The HTTP API is served under the `/api` prefix on the same origin.
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready.
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps.
Login credentials are written to `/app/USER_README.md`.
The directory `.browser_screenshots/` exists at the app root, empty.
The app serves a production build behind a static or preview server.
The server keeps running after the session ends.
The server binds `0.0.0.0` rather than a loopback address.
The app starts no copy of a backing service named in the brief.
The app uses no persistent volume.
A list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array ...
An in-memory store standing in for the bucket is a violation of the contract.
